reader_profile.age_rule: Premise and narrative maturity must fit exact age independently from vocabulary difficulty.

character.name: Deniz
character.starting_goal: earn the right to chart routes beyond the home strait and prove that careful observation can reveal things official maps miss
starting_relationships: a close friend who prefers practical experiments to theories
a demanding mapmaker who respects evidence more than confidence
harbor crews who know Deniz as a serious apprentice rather than a passenger

world.era: age of sail with precision mechanical navigation
world.habitat: a vast island chain divided by deep channels, storm belts and partially mapped outer seas
world.technology_level: sailing ships, mechanical clocks, optical instruments, printing presses and hand-built navigation devices
world.magic_level: rare, rule-bound geophysical phenomena associated with tides, magnetic stone and ancient infrastructure; no arbitrary spellcasting
world.summary: The Shattered Meridian is an archipelago civilization whose survival depends on maps. Most inner routes are well known, but outer charts disagree, old observatories stand on remote islands, drowned roads appear at extreme tides, and some navigation markers predate every living culture. The world rewards exploration, evidence and careful inference rather than effortless magic.
locations: Meridian Harbor, Deniz's known home port
Beacon Ridge, a chain of signal towers above the inner strait
the Drowned Causeway, visible only during rare low tides
the Outer Mist Line, where official charts become incomplete
an abandoned tide observatory on a distant mapped island
social_context: cartographers and navigators hold respected public roles
island councils depend on reliable sea routes
young apprentices may take meaningful expedition roles within established safety rules
merchant captains, fishers and scholars often disagree about what counts as trustworthy evidence
old folklore sometimes preserves real geographic information in distorted form
known_pressures: several navigation beacons no longer agree with official charts
outer-island routes are becoming economically important
storm season will eventually restrict long voyages
different groups have reasons to prefer different versions of the map

test_intents: age-12 premise maturity must come from story substance rather than difficult vocabulary
long-horizon Main Saga with 5-7 anchors and 15-30 meaningful milestones
multiple routes and optional Saga dormancy

compactness_rules: Set milestone_target_count values so their sum is exactly 15.
Do not generate individual milestone details yet.
Keep each narrative field concise, normally one sentence.
Do not repeat schema definitions or explain reasoning outside JSON.

origin.summary: Deniz grew up on the docks of Meridian Harbor, learning to read tide tables and beacon signals before learning to read books.
origin_facts: Deniz is a formally registered apprentice under a demanding master mapmaker.
Deniz's family has crewed harbor ferries for two generations but never sailed beyond the inner strait.
Deniz first noticed a beacon misalignment at Beacon Ridge that official charts ignored.
formative_events: Deniz once corrected a minor chart error that a harbor pilot had missed, earning quiet respect.
Deniz was scolded for taking an unauthorized skiff out near the Drowned Causeway at low tide.
origin_relationships: A close friend who tests Deniz's theories with practical rigging and instrument experiments.
A demanding mapmaker mentor who only trusts verified evidence over confident claims.
Harbor crews who treat Deniz as a serious, if junior, working apprentice.
unresolved_origin_questions: Why do certain beacon markers predate every known culture in the archipelago?
Did Deniz's family avoid outer routes by choice or because of something unspoken?

present_situation.summary: Deniz is on the edge of being trusted with real charting responsibility, just as several official beacons begin disagreeing with the maps they're supposed to support.
present_situation.current_status: Apprentice cartographer with limited independent authority, seeking a qualifying expedition assignment.
immediate_pressures: Storm season will soon close off long-range voyages for the year.
Rival chart-makers want their version of the outer routes adopted first.
open_threads: The Drowned Causeway only appears at rare tides and seems to lead somewhere unmapped.
Beacon Ridge signals no longer match the official chart set Deniz was trained on.

narrative_core.core_tension: Trusting careful, patient observation versus the pressure to produce fast, convenient answers that powerful people want.
narrative_core.wonder_engine: Ancient, rule-bound geography (drowned roads, mismatched beacons, pre-cultural markers) that rewards curiosity with real discoveries rather than magic.
narrative_core.agency_engine: Deniz's choices about which evidence to trust, which routes to chart, and who to ally with materially change what parts of the world become accessible.
narrative_core.mystery_engine: The disagreement between official charts and physical reality points to something deliberately hidden in the archipelago's geography and history.

main_saga.title: The True Chart of the Shattered Meridian
main_saga.goal: Discover why the official charts and the physical world no longer agree, and produce a chart trustworthy enough to change how the archipelago navigates its future.
main_saga.stakes: Whoever controls the accepted chart controls trade routes, safety, and reputation across the islands — a wrong or captured chart could strand ships or hand advantage to the wrong hands.
main_saga.central_mystery: What is the true source and purpose of the beacon markers and drowned roads that predate every living culture in the Meridian?
themes: the sea as a keeper of old secrets

anchors.title: The Qualifying Discrepancy
anchors.purpose: Establish Deniz's credibility and formally surface the beacon/chart mismatch as a real problem worth investigating.
anchors.target_state: Deniz is authorized to investigate discrepancies as part of an apprentice trial, with mentor oversight.

anchors.title: The Drowned Causeway Opens
anchors.purpose: Give Deniz physical access to a route unknown to official charts, expanding the map of what's possible.
anchors.target_state: Deniz has personally traced and documented a stretch of the Drowned Causeway, gaining a route no rival chart-maker has.

anchors.title: The Observatory's Testimony
anchors.purpose: Provide verified historical evidence connecting the beacon mismatches to a deliberate, older navigational system.
anchors.target_state: Deniz has recovered and partially decoded old observatory records that hint at the beacons' true origin and purpose.

anchors.title: Competing Charts, Competing Claims
anchors.purpose: Introduce social and political stakes as rival cartographers and captains push their own versions of the truth.
anchors.target_state: Deniz's findings are publicly contested, forcing choices about which allies and methods to rely on.

anchors.title: The New Chart is Proposed
anchors.purpose: Bring evidence and reputation together into a chart credible enough to be considered for real adoption.
anchors.target_state: Deniz presents a revised chart backed by verified evidence, changing formal navigation practice in at least one region.

anchor_edges.rationale: Deniz may choose to pursue physical exploration of the Causeway as the primary path to evidence.
Deniz may instead choose historical/documentary investigation as the primary path to evidence.
A newly charted route attracts rival attention and competing claims.
Historical evidence invites public scrutiny and competing interpretations.
Deniz must navigate social conflict before a new chart can gain enough credibility to be proposed.
Physical route evidence strengthens the eventual chart proposal.
Historical evidence strengthens the eventual chart proposal.

hidden_truths.statement: The oldest beacon markers were built by a pre-archipelago seafaring culture to mark safe passage through a now-shifted magnetic-stone field, not by any known island culture.
Whether the Drowned Causeway was originally a road, a boundary marker, or something else entirely remains genuinely undetermined for future development.
Deniz's grandparent once sailed past the Outer Mist Line and returned with a damaged instrument and a vow of silence, which is why the family avoided outer routes.
Whether the rival cartographers' resistance is driven by genuine belief, profit, or fear of what the true chart reveals is left open.

reveal_intents.summary: Observatory records suggest the beacons are far older than any known culture.
reveal_intents.eligibility: After Deniz has recovered at least partial observatory records.

reveal_intents.summary: Cross-referenced evidence confirms the beacons predate every living culture and mark a magnetic-stone corridor.
reveal_intents.eligibility: Only after both causeway and observatory evidence anchors are complete.

reveal_intents.summary: A harbor elder alludes to Deniz's grandparent once returning from the outer seas changed and silent.
reveal_intents.eligibility: Anytime after anchor_apprentice_trial, as optional flavor.

reveal_intents.summary: Physical traces on the Causeway raise more questions about its original purpose than they answer.
A rival's private conversation suggests their motives are more complicated than pure profit.

latent_side_sagas.seed_summary: Deniz's practical-minded friend wants to build a mechanical device to test theories the official instruments can't, creating a parallel path of trust and invention.
latent_side_sagas.possible_intersection_with_main: The device could later verify or challenge observatory findings.

latent_side_sagas.seed_summary: Local folklore about the outer seas may encode real geographic information distorted through generations of storytelling.
latent_side_sagas.possible_intersection_with_main: Could provide an alternative, less formal evidence source for the true chart.

latent_side_sagas.seed_summary: The demanding mapmaker mentor has an unexplained past failure with an outer expedition that shaped their strict standards.
latent_side_sagas.possible_intersection_with_main: Could deepen or complicate the mentor relationship during rival pressure conflicts.

latent_side_sagas.seed_summary: Unusual migration patterns of a known sea creature species near the Mist Line could hint at environmental changes worth separate investigation.
latent_side_sagas.possible_intersection_with_main: Could later tie into why beacons and tides are shifting.

future_architects_may_propose: new minor NPCs, harbor locations, and rival factions consistent with the world
additional side sagas that intersect but do not override the Main Saga
alternate emotional framings of existing relationships
new folklore or historical fragments consistent with FIXED_HIDDEN truths
future_architects_may_not_propose: resolving FIXED_HIDDEN truths ahead of eligibility
forcing a specific route choice as already made
assuming character trust, alliance, or forgiveness decisions in advance
creative_permission_envelope.durable_fact_commit_rule: All durable facts require a validated outcome commit; proposals remain non-canon until then.

reweave_policy.dormancy_notes: Many Episodes may focus on harbor life, side sagas, or unrelated adventures without advancing the Main Saga.
reactivation_triggers: a new beacon discrepancy is reported
a rival cartographer makes a public claim
Deniz encounters causeway or observatory evidence incidentally
callback_requirements: Early NPCs and locations should be eligible to reappear with added context.
Symbols or instruments introduced early may gain new meaning later.
Failures or unresolved threads should be able to resurface as consequences.

constraints: Passive enrichment must not resolve FIXED_HIDDEN truths.
Passive enrichment must not answer UNRESOLVED_BY_DESIGN questions.
Passive enrichment should favor sensory, cultural, or minor factual texture over plot-critical revelations.

safety_and_constraints.age_appropriate_stakes: Physical risk exists (tides, storms, remote islands) but is bounded by mentorship, safety rules, and no permanent-injury outcomes without human review.
prohibited_content: graphic violence or peril beyond adventure-appropriate tension
irreversible character death without explicit human approval
agency_protections: No future Episode may pre-decide Deniz's trust, alliance, or route choices.
Any resolution of central mystery elements requires validated outcome commit, not narrative assumption.
